row.name: Children's Center of Excellence and Daycare

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting, Firm, Flat Mattress Designed for Use in Crib: A 7 month old infant was observed sleeping in a crib with two additional mattresses under the original mattress.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting, Firm, Flat Mattress Designed for Use in Crib (26 TAC §746.2409(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Requirements during probation: Probation condition #6 was not fully satisfied due to the following information not being available for review for all staff including the director.    A training information sheet which lists each of the following:  -name and role (director, caregiver, cook, driver)  -original hire date  -current training timeframe  -date CPR/FA training completed  -date orientation training completed  -date pre-service training completed (or exemption)  -number of training hours remaining to satisfy the current year?s requirements  -specific topics remaining to satisfy the current year?s requirements (per 746.1309, 746.1311)
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements during probation (26 TAC §745.8641)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, children are made to put their heads down on the table for a period of 5-10 minutes. If anyone is heard talking, the time will restart, or additional minutes will be added for all children. Children who are not misbehaving or those who arrive to the operation after timeout has begun are also required to put their heads down until the time has ended.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2805(10))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, there is sufficient information to support the allegation regarding staff yelling at children. Based on the information obtained, staff yell at children to sit down, be quiet or stop talking.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training: Records were reviewed for 10 staff. 2 caregiver with less than 2 years of child care experience hired June and July 2023, did not have the required 24 hours of training within 90 days of employment. 1 caregiver with no previous experience had documentation of training.    NOTE: Caregivers hired June and July of 2023 had 8 hours of pre-service training documented.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Caregiver Qualification Age Exemption Attends High School - Supervised By Qualified Caregiver: A 17 yr old caregiver who currently attends high school was observed to be left unsupervised with a group of children multiple times. The supervising caregiver was observed to be going back and forth between the kitchen and classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Caregiver Qualification Age Exemption Attends High School - Supervised By Qualified Caregiver (26 TAC §746.1109(b)(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records: Records for 10 staff including the director was reviewed. All records were observed to be missing the following:    Date of hire  Documentation whether pre-service training be required.  Documentation all required orientation topics have been received.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records (26 TAC §746.801(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device: A caregiver placed a child in a high chair for misbehaving during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2805(10))

occurrences.finding: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer: Children were observed sitting in high chairs and the safety straps were not secured.    Note: The provider secured the straps for each child during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer (26 TAC §746.4501(b))

occurrences.finding: Smoke Detectors Testing: Documentation showing the smoke detectors have been tested monthly was not available for review upon request.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Smoke Detectors Testing (26 TAC §746.5319)

occurrences.finding: Medication No Longer Used: During the inspection expired boxes of Benadryl and Neosporin ointment was observed and has not been disposed of.    Note: The provider disposed the medication during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Medication No Longer Used (26 TAC §746.3809)

occurrences.finding: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer: Children were observed sitting in chairs equipped with safety straps and the safety straps were not secured.    Note: The provider secured the straps for each child during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer (26 TAC §746.4501(b))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: 1 out of 4 chidlren's files evaluated did not contain documentation of current immunizations. The record provided was missing 1 dose of MMR and 1 dose of VAR.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Check All Detectors Monthly: Documentation showing the carbon monoxide detectors are being tested monthly was not available for review upon request.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Check All Detectors Monthly (26 TAC §746.5537(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Training Requirements - Original Training Certification Card or Letter in each Employee's personnel record: Documentation showing training in the following topics were not available for review during the inspection:    - Recognizing and Reporting Suspected Abuse and Neglect of Children  - Transportation Safety Training
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Training Requirements - Original Training Certification Card or Letter in each Employee's personnel record (26 TAC §746.1329(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records: 7 out of 8 staff files evaluated did not contain a complete personnel record. The following information was missing:    4 were missing the Licensing affidavits were not notarized  2 were missing the Proof of education was missing  3 were missing Signatures that the staff have completed orientation to the center
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.901)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: Children's files evaluated did not contain a complete record. The following information was missing or incomplete:    - Two were missing the address, and phone # of the emergency medical facility  - Three were missing the special needs statements  - Two were missing the parents signature for receiving a copy of the operational policies
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operational policies were evaluated and did not contain the following information:    - A Safe Sleeping Policy for Infants Under 12 months  - The benefits of physical activity and outdoor play  - The duration of physical activity at your operation, both indoor and outdoor  - The type of physical activity (structured and unstructured) that children may engage in at your operation  - Each setting in which your physical activity program will take place  - The criteria you will use to determine when extreme weather conditions pose a significant health risk that prohibits or limits outdoor play and    - A plan to ensure physical activity occurs on days when extreme weather conditions prohibit or limit outdoor play.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric CPR: 1 out of 8 employee files evaluated did not contain current CPR/First Aid training. The certifiate provided had expired on May 4th, 2023.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(4)(A))

occurrences.finding: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness: The operation did not report an outbreak of hand, foot, and mouth to childcare regulation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness (26 TAC §746.305(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions: A caregiver with a conditonal background check stating they must never be left alone with child was left alone with 6 infant 4-15mo
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions (26 TAC §745.635(3))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A caregiver was observed leaving a classroom multiple times during the inspection. The caregiver left another caregiver alone to supervise a total of 14 children 20m-2yrs old. Based on the specified age group (SAG) of the classroom was 2yrs. The caregiver was over ratio by 3    Upon arrival 3 caregiver were observed in the infant room, two caregiver then left the room. One infant caregiver was observed with 6 infants 4-15 mo. The SAG for the group was 0-11mo. The caregiver was over ratio by 2 for approx. 5-10 munites before the caregiver returned.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: One child not yet on table food did not have  updated feeding instructions. Instructions were last reviewed and signed by the parent 2/1/23
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: The operation does not keep a sign-in/out log for children being transported.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: First Aid Kit - Easily Accessible to Employees: The first aid kit was observed to be located in the truck of the vehicle used for transportation and was not readily accessible by the driver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: First Aid Kit - Easily Accessible to Employees (26 TAC §746.4001(3))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Fire Extinguisher: The fire extinguisher was observed to be located in the trunk of the vehicle used for transportation and was not readily accessible by the driver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Fire Extinguisher (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information: The vehicle used for transportation did not have emergency medical authorization for any of the children being transported.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for: 2 caregivers in the infant room were not aware of the number of children in their care. When asked, both caregivers stated there were 5 children in care. When asked again, they again stated there were 5. The caregivers were informed CCR counted 6 children. One careigver then stated they forgot a child was just brought into the classroom
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: Based on the information obtained during the DFPS investigation, the operation failed to report a child injury that required medical treatment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: Based on the information obtained during the DFPS investigation, the operation failed to ensure the areas were free of all safety hazards. A bottle warmer was stored in a manner that did not ensure the cord was out of reach of the children, resulting in a child injury.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: 2 caregivers were not aware of the number of children in their care. When asked, both caregivers were asked multiple times how many children were in their care, and both stated there were 15. 16 children were counted in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For (26 TAC §746.1203(2))

occurrences.finding: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer: 14 children were observed sitting in bucket seat style tables and the straps were not observed to be in use. Two of the seats did not have straps.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer (26 TAC §746.4501(b))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: During the walkthrough, in the infant, toddler, and school age rooms, staff purses were observed to be in reach of children    NOTE: Corrected at inspection, all purses were moved to high hooks or shelved and were out of  reach of children
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Storage of Medication - Refrigerate Separate from Food: Refrigerated medication was observed to be stored next to food.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Storage of Medication - Refrigerate Separate from Food (26 TAC §746.3807(3))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: Two infants not yet on table food did not have updated feeding instructions. Feeding instructions for one child was last completed 5/2022. Feeding instructions for another child was not dated, caregivers were not aware of when the instructions were written.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits: In the toddler room, a child was observed to be sleeping on a cot that was placed in front of the emergency exit. The exit could not be accessed without stepping over the child
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits (26 TAC §746.2909(1))

occurrences.finding: Additional Minimum Qualifications for Caregivers - HS Diploma, Equivalent, Certification of Completion: One caregiver did not have documentation of a high school diploma or equivalent on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Additional Minimum Qualifications for Caregivers - HS Diploma, Equivalent, Certification of Completion (26 TAC §746.1107(2))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training - Caregivers of Children Under 24 Months Required: Records were reviewed for 6 staff including the director, three caregivers did not have training in the following topics:    Hazardous materials  Building and physical premise safety  Emergency preparedness  Responding to food and allergic reaction
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training - Caregivers of Children Under 24 Months Required (26 TAC §746.1309(d))

occurrences.finding: Minimum Qualifications Child Care Center Employees and Caregivers - Affidavit: Records were reviewed for 6 staff including the director. 5 staff did not have a notarized affidavit on file
occurrences.violation_type_title: Minimum Qualifications Employees and Caregivers - Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.1105(3))

occurrences.finding: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes: 2 infants between 0-11 mo were observed sitting in a baby swing and bouncer for more than 15 mintues.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes (26 TAC §746.2417(2)(B))

occurrences.finding: Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: A container of diaper rash cream was observed in the crib with an 19mo old.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3807(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device: A 3mo old was observed sleeping in a baby swing. The caregiver was unaware that the infant was sleep. The infant was removed after instructed by CCR.    According to the caregiver, the infants were in the restrictive devices for at least 20 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2426)

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A caregiver was observed with 8 children 3-21 months. The SAG was 0-11  mo. The caregiver was overratio by 4 children
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages: A caregiver was unaware of the ages of children in their care. When asked for the ages, the caregiver stated they guessed the age of the child and then stated they were unsure and did not want to say the wrong thing
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages (26 TAC §746.1203(3))

occurrences.finding: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers: A 19 mo old toddler was observed sleep in a crib with toys.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2501(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: The caregiver was observed with 11 children. When asked for the number of children in care there were 10 children present
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For (26 TAC §746.1203(2))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: An infant was observed in a crib with a broken wheel. The crib was observed to be slanted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance: Sign-in/out logs for the director was requested and was not made available for review. According to the owner, a log of attendance for the director is not kept.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance (26 TAC §746.801(5))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A caregiver was observed with 11 children 4-23 months. The SAG was 18-23 mo. The caregiver was overratio by 3 children
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages: A caregiver was unaware of the ages of children in their care. When asked for the ages, the caregiver stated they had just arrived and did not know.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages (26 TAC §746.1203(3))

occurrences.finding: Director Presence Routine During Operating Hours: The director is only present at the operation two days a week and is not routinely present during the hours of operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Presence Routine During Operating Hours (26 TAC §746.1011)

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - Combining Ages With 12 or Fewer Children: There were 4 children ages 4m-15 mo old observed with children 18-23 mo. There were 24 total children in the building.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - Combining Ages With 12 or Fewer Children (26 TAC §746.1703)

occurrences.finding: Director Presence Routine During Operating Hours: The director is only present at the operation two days a week and is not routinely present during the hours of operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Presence Routine During Operating Hours (26 TAC §746.1011)

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance: Sign-in/out logs for the director was requested and was not made available for review. According to the owner, a log of attendance for the director is not kept.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance (26 TAC §746.801(5))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Cleaning chemicals in a spray bottle were observed on the table in reach of children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Children in Control: Several children were observed crawing under tables in the eating area. The children were observed crawling under the table for approx. 3 mintues before the caregivers were aware.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children (26 TAC §746.1203(5))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, as a result of the director's frequent absence, the director was unaware of  the caregivers' activities prior to and when engaging in a physical altercation. The director failed to ensure all staff were supervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised (26 TAC §746.1003(4))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: based on the information obtained during the investigation, incident reports were not created for the 6 children present and placed at risk when two caregivers had a physical altercation
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on he information obtained during the investigation, 2 caregivers engaged in a physical and verbal altercation with children present resulting in two children being pushed over chairs.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, parents were not notified immediately that there was a situation that placed their children at risk.  NOTE" Two parents were notified immediately, other parents were not notified until pick-up.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022 revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22, 2022 as required.    NOTE: The operation reported the number of employees who left in 2021 after the deadline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: Transportation training for the director was not made available for review.    NOTE: Training for the owner/driver was reviewed and up-to-date
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Telephone Numbers for Each Child: The operation did not have parent contacts or emergnecy contacts for 13 of the 23 of the children being transported.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Telephone Numbers for Each Child (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(4))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: A play equipment with a height less than 5 feet did not have at least 6 inches of surfacing
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The operation did not have a current fire inspection available for review. The last fire inspection was conducted 1/19/21
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products- Annual Certification (26 TAC §746.4135(b))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(1))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - First-aid Kit (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(6))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Telephone Numbers for Each Child (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(4))

NOTE: According to the owner, transportation began the second week of January 2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Notification of Additional Services Offered (26 TAC §746.301(7))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))
